newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary opposition KDNP parliament group dissolved.
newsitem.headline: Hungary opposition KDNP parliament group dissolved.

text.p: The parliamentary group of Hungary's opposition Christian Democratic Party (KDNP) has dissolved after seven members announced on Monday they were quitting the group, Hungarian Television said,
The defections reduced the number of members to below the minimum for formal recognition of a parliamentary grouping, the television quoted KDNP spokesman Ildiko Laszlo as saying.

The European Union of Christian Democrats (EUCD) expelled the KDNP a week ago for failing to end internal divisions and sever all ties with Hungary's extreme right, and for not seeking co-operation with centre-right parties.

Following the EUCD decision, three MPs were expelled from the then 23-member parliamentary faction last week, and three more including party president Gyorgy Giczy walked out. The latest seven to leave announced their departure at a party meeting on Monday.
There are 386 seats in Hungary's parliament. Seventy-two percent of them are held by a coalition between Socialists and the liberal Free Democrats.
